subsystems.name: Expanded genetic alphabet
subsystems.role: stores information in unnatural base pairs (UBPs) alongside A-T and G-C.
parts: polymerases that read and copy them

subsystems.name: Orthogonal translation machinery
subsystems.role: incorporates non-standard amino acids (nsAAs) into proteins at defined positions.

subsystems.name: Metabolic supply
subsystems.role: provides the cell with the unnatural nucleotides and amino acids it needs to grow.
parts: biosynthetic pathways or transporters for UBPs

subsystems.name: Containment and safety
subsystems.role: prevents the synthetic organism from surviving outside the lab.

subsystems.name: Chassis genome
subsystems.role: a host cell engineered to tolerate and maintain the expanded chemistry.

buildSteps.title: Design unnatural base pairs
buildSteps.detail: Chemists create nucleotide analogues that pair stably and are recognised by DNA and RNA polymerases, avoiding mispairing with natural bases.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise building blocks
buildSteps.detail: The unnatural nucleotides and non-standard amino acids are made in the lab and tested for stability and low toxicity.

buildSteps.title: Engineer uptake or synthesis
buildSteps.detail: Genes are added so the chassis cell can import the unnatural nucleotides or make them from cheaper precursors.

buildSteps.title: Insert expanded information
buildSteps.detail: The UBP is placed into a plasmid or the chromosome using genome-editing tools, and the cell is selected for retaining it.

buildSteps.title: Evolve orthogonal translation
buildSteps.detail: Directed evolution selects tRNA/synthetase pairs that reliably insert a non-standard amino acid in response to a unique codon.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise replication and inheritance
buildSteps.detail: Polymerases and repair systems are tuned so the UBP is not lost over many generations.

buildSteps.title: Add containment
buildSteps.detail: The organism is made dependent on a synthetic nutrient so it cannot escape and survive.

buildSteps.title: Test in extreme conditions
buildSteps.detail: The chassis is exposed to radiation, solvents, heat or salt to see whether the new chemistry confers a survival advantage.

prerequisites.why: you must write and read the expanded genetic code accurately.

prerequisites.tech: Unnatural base pair replication in living cells
prerequisites.why: one or two UBPs have been maintained in E. coli since 2014, but not yet in a robust free-living organism.
they allow non-standard amino acids to be inserted into proteins, but only a few at a time.
cells must be fed the unnatural building blocks or be engineered to make them.
synthetic auxotrophy and kill switches work in the lab but are not proven at scale.
we know some natural proteins survive harsh conditions, but we cannot yet design a whole synthetic chassis for them.

pathway.milestone: semi-synthetic E. coli that maintains a single unnatural base pair
pathway.unlocks: proof that expanded DNA can be replicated inside a living cell.

pathway.milestone: organisms with multiple UBPs and several non-standard amino acids in their proteins
pathway.unlocks: proteins with new chemical functions, such as better catalysts or sensors.

pathway.milestone: a contained chassis that cannot survive without lab-made nutrients
pathway.unlocks: safe laboratory and industrial use of xenobiology.
bioremediation or sensing in radiation, high salt or organic solvents — still speculative.
